entries.definition: Right-living. God is Right-Living by definition — His ways and works are the measure of right. For those under His authority, right-living is the doing of His commandments: the law kept, worn as the garment of righteous acts. Romans 4 excludes wage-work that would put God in debt, not obedience; even complete obedience earns no wage because the servant has only done his duty. Righteousness is given and reckoned by grace, but the gift never renames wrong-living right.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: primarily right standing before God — Christ's imputed righteousness received by faith apart from works — with right-living as its subsequent fruit and evidence.
entries.citations: (Deut 32:4; 6:25; Ps 119:172; 145:17; Luke 17:7-10; Rom 4:4-8; Phil 3:9; Heb 11:8; 1 John 3:7) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6, for the dependent definitions; The End of the Law for Paul's wage, debt, law, and obedience vocabulary; and Garments & Armor, ch. 43, for righteousness given and worn
